title: Tech Note: Optimization and new cache management for 4D 2004
author: 4D S.A.
featured_technology: 4D cache/memory management (address tables, index pages, records)
FLUSH BUFFER command and cache flushing
SET DATABASE PARAMETER (cache write optimization selector)

historical_commentary.text: This note explains 4D 2004's rewritten cache/memory management system, including reduced fragmentation at large cache sizes, faster cache-flush write throughput, and faster record loading via OS-level system cache reuse, alongside guidance on sizing the cache using Runtime Explorer hit-ratio statistics. The conceptual guidance on cache sizing (keep index/address tables cached, size for record hit ratio, avoid cache thrashing) remains generally sound database performance thinking, but the specific 2003-vs-2004 comparisons, hardware figures (Mb/s, RAM sizes), and mentioned 32-bit-era cache-size ceilings (up to 1 Gb) are firmly dated to mid-2000s hardware and 4D internals.
related_updates: 4D's cache/memory management has continued to evolve substantially since 2004, including support for far larger memory configurations on modern 64-bit systems
The Runtime Explorer and FLUSH BUFFER-based cache monitoring/tuning concepts described are largely still present in spirit in current 4D, though with updated implementations
